deviations.detail: The worklist derives expected_tag from the NEW TRANSLATED slug, but /api/revalidate builds the product tag from the slug the request carries — and the request carries the BASE slug, as the worklist itself specifies. So the endpoint emits product:{channel}:{locale}:{base_slug} and can never emit the translated form for this request. The purge still reaches the entry behind the translated URL: a foreign PDP is tagged with BOTH its URL slug and its base slug (src/lib/saleor/product-cache-tags.ts). Measured on all three AT cells — after a base-slug event the next request recomputed (479/856/451 ms) against 12-14 ms served from cache. Drop this check from the next worklist or set expected_tag to the base-slug form.

revalidateTag does not take effect for a request issued immediately after the endpoint responds. With no settle only 2/33 recomputed, with 250 ms 1/33, with 2 s every cell tested recomputed. Allow ~2 s before treating a response as post-purge when the remaining 100694 cells are swapped.

notes: The new URLs already served 200 before this revalidation ran: the cached not-found answers from M's own pre-swap probes had already been refreshed. Nothing was blocked; the worklist was still run in full.
Identity is compared after stripping the cfm:product: prefix, the same rule the proxy uses in sameCfmProduct(); Saleor stores externalReference as cfm:product:CFMP-…
Old URLs return one 301 straight to the final path — the second hop is the 200, never another redirect.
